reader.requirement: For a Format 2 (RECORD IS VARYING) sequential file, the size of each record description is the sum of its elementary items' character positions excluding REDEFINES and RENAMES (plus any implementor slack for SYNCHRONIZED), with an OCCURS DEPENDING table counted at its minimum occurrences for the minimum size and at its maximum for the maximum size; these sizes feed GR6/GR7's default bounds.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize: whether a Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5 binds WRITE/REWRITE sizes (off at 1985); a Format 2 RECORD IS VARYING clause sets BoundsEnforced true at every edition

reader.edition-search: Grepped FileModel.cs, DataItem.cs, FileControlBinder*.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs and the runtime IO directory for DialectLevel/Edition/DialectBehavior/IsActive; the size summations (MinExtent, MaxRecordSize, ByteWidth) and VaryMin/VaryMax read no edition; the runtime bound test (OutsideVaryingBounds) reads none; the registration passes the edition to the connector, where only CLOSE WITH LOCK, sharing and the indexed arms read it.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f18_02 covers REDEFINES and RENAMES exclusion and a top-level ODO table at its minimum and maximum; not covered: an ODO of a group with several elementary items (probe rv1 R2), a SYNCHRONIZED item (WiseOwl lays no slack, ItemLength/BitLayout), a maximum from an ODO exceeding every other record (rv1 G2)

probes.expected: F: no integers; records X(10), N+GRP(3) OCCURS 1 TO 3 (min 4, max 10), P X(6)+Q REDEFINES P+S X(2) SYNC (8): min 4 (GR5a, GR6), max 10 (GR5b, GR7): 3 and 11 are 44, 4, 10, 8 succeed. G: FROM 2, no TO; G1 X(5), G2 1+X(3) OCCURS 2 TO 5 (max 16): 1 is 44, 2 and 16 succeed, 17 is 44 (GR7 over an ODO maximum)
the Format 2 rule is unchanged in substance; the 1985 arm is the 2023 arm

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR5  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: MinExtent sums non-redefining children at MinimumOccurrences (ODO integer-1), MaxRecordSize is ByteWidth (ODO at its maximum, redefinitions skipped); a 66-level RENAMES adds no storage. The implicit FILLER for synchronization is zero because WiseOwl lays no SYNCHRONIZED padding (implementor latitude, documented in ItemLength.cs), so the SYNC record of rv1 is 8.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-121/src/rvr1.cob (rvr1-002) at --std 85. File H: RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE with no integers and no DEPENDING ON (GR10 c path, not the reader's data-name-1 path); records H1 X(10), H2 = N PIC 9 + HG(X(2)+X) OCCURS 0 TO 3 (0 is legal, §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR5) with a 66 RENAMES, H3 = 9(4) COMP + X(4): WRITE H2 at N=0 (1 position) 00, N=3 (10) 00, H3 00, H1 00; read back through a second FD with DEPENDING ON: lengths 1,10,6,10 (status 04 there is that FD's own GR6 minimum of 10). File K: TO 12, no FROM, least record K2 (COMP+X(4)=6) under K1 X(8): L=1..5 are 44, 6..9 are 00. The minimum sums a zero-occurrence ODO group, a RENAMES adds nothing, a COMP item counts at its implementor size, and the least record is chosen across records. SYNCHRONIZED slack is the implementor's and documented (docs/conformance/7). cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR5a; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR6; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR7; OK §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR5. (A first run, rvr1-001, had a PIC 9 loop counter that could not exceed 9; it was stopped before writing any K record and rerun with PIC 99.)
